data.title: Identification of Sin1 as an essential TORC2 component required for complex formation and kinase activity
data.authors: Yang Q; Guan KL et al.

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: Identified Sin1 as an essential TORC2 component required for Akt phosphorylation.
data.abstract_excerpt: Target of rapamycin (TOR) is an evolutionally conserved protein kinase in eukaryotes and a central cell growth controller. TOR exists in two distinct complexes, termed TORC1 and TORC2. Mammalian TORC2 has recently been shown to possess kinase activity toward the C-terminal hydrophobic site of Akt/PKB. Here, we report that Sin1 is an essential component of TORC2 but not of TORC1, and functions similarly to Rictor, the defining member of TORC2, in complex formation and kinase activity.

extracted_findings.effect: Sin1 is an essential TORC2 component required for complex formation and kinase activity toward Akt
